boundary: Hospital ownership of the patient referenced by a child write

local_checks.invariant: Every clinical child write must verify that the referenced patient belongs to the session hospital.
local_checks.result: Four handlers use the URL patient ID without a hospital-scoped ownership lookup; Prisma relations enforce only patient ID existence.

local_checks.invariant: A patient ID from a request cannot cross the hospital boundary without a matching session tenant.
local_checks.result: Independent source verification confirmed the missing ownership check and contrasted nearby properly scoped patient and triage handlers.

unresolved: The source-level missing check is verified, but no bounded local dummy-tenant write was run to confirm runtime/database effects.

boundary: Role assignment and tenant-safe user mutation

local_checks.invariant: Only authorized managers may create, promote, modify, or delete hospital users; request fields cannot change tenant scope.
local_checks.result: The plural API checks only session, accepts cargo on create, and spreads the full PUT body after an ownership check; singular handler has an ADMIN check.

local_checks.invariant: Role and hospital claims must be authorized and derived at the server-side mutation boundary.
local_checks.result: Independent verification confirmed body-controlled role promotion and hospitalId mutation through the plural endpoints, used by the user UI.

unresolved: No local dummy-user mutation was executed; session refresh and deployed reachability details remain unverified.

boundary: Role authorization for hospital-shared dashboard module settings

local_checks.invariant: Only authorized administrators may mutate hospital-shared module visibility; client-side password unlocks are not server authorization.
local_checks.result: The configuration POST checks for a session and scopes by hospital but has no ADMIN check; the support-password gate only unlocks UI state.

unresolved: Source confirms missing role enforcement; no isolated local authorization test was possible. The support-password fallback is active only if the deployment variable is absent.
